title: A community photography course
instructions: Listen to the dialogue and answer three questions. This short exercise is not a full IELTS test.
content: Receptionist: Hello, Riverside Learning Centre. How can I help? Student: I'd like to join the photography course. Receptionist: The next course begins on Tuesday the fourteenth of May. Classes run from six to eight in the evening. Student: How much does it cost? Receptionist: Eighty-five pounds for six weeks. Please bring your own camera. Student: Where do we meet? Receptionist: In room twelve, on the first floor.

questions.prompt: Which month does the course begin?
questions.explanation: The receptionist says the fourteenth of May.

questions.prompt: How much does the six-week course cost in pounds?
questions.explanation: The full course costs eighty-five pounds.

questions.prompt: What room number is used?
questions.explanation: The class meets in room twelve.

title: The value of urban trees
instructions: Read the passage and answer TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN using only the passage.
content: Urban trees offer more than an attractive view. Their leaves provide shade, which can reduce the temperature of pavements during hot weather. Trees also intercept some rainfall before it reaches the ground. However, planting a tree is only the beginning: young trees need regular care, especially during dry periods. One neighbourhood project asked volunteers to water newly planted trees each week throughout their first summer. The organisers reported that residents enjoyed working together, but they did not measure changes in local air quality. The project used several tree species rather than relying on a single variety. This approach was intended to reduce the risk that one disease would affect every tree.

questions.prompt: Shade from trees can make pavements cooler in hot weather.
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly says shade can reduce pavement temperatures.

questions.prompt: The project planted only one variety of tree.
questions.explanation: The project used several tree species.

questions.prompt: The project improved local air quality by twenty percent.
questions.explanation: Air-quality changes were not measured and no percentage is supplied.

title: Academic Task 2: transport priorities
instructions: Allow 40 minutes and aim for at least 250 words. Self-review is not an official band assessment.
content: Some people believe governments should spend more money on public transport than on building new roads. To what extent do you agree or disagree? Give reasons for your answer and include relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

title: Part 2: a useful skill
instructions: Prepare for one minute, then speak for one to two minutes. Use the recording feature in the downloaded site to review your response.
content: Describe a useful skill you learned. You should say: what the skill is; when and how you learned it; why you decided to learn it; and explain how it has helped you. Follow-up questions: Why is lifelong learning important? Should schools focus more on practical skills? How has technology changed the way people learn?

title: Joining a local library
instructions: Listen without opening the transcript. Write no more than two words and/or a number for each answer. Original short practice, not a full IELTS examination.
content: Librarian: Welcome to Brookside Library. Membership is free for local residents. Visitor: What should I bring? Librarian: A photo identification card and a recent bill showing your address. You can borrow eight books at a time. Visitor: How long can I keep them? Librarian: For three weeks. We close at seven on weekdays, but at four on Saturdays. Our conversation club meets every Thursday in the garden room. Visitor: Is there a fee? Librarian: No, the club is free too.

questions.prompt: How many books can a member borrow?
questions.explanation: The librarian allows eight books at a time.

questions.prompt: For how many weeks can books be borrowed?
questions.explanation: The borrowing period is three weeks.

questions.prompt: At what hour does the library close on Saturdays?
questions.explanation: Saturday closing is at four.

questions.prompt: On which day does the conversation club meet?
questions.explanation: The club meets every Thursday.

questions.prompt: What room does the club use?
questions.explanation: The meeting place is the garden room.

title: A coastal field trip
instructions: Listen without opening the transcript. Write no more than two words and/or a number for each answer. Original short practice, not a full IELTS examination.
content: Guide: Our coach leaves the college at nine tomorrow morning. Please arrive fifteen minutes early. We will visit the coastal research station, not the museum as originally planned. The journey takes forty minutes. You should bring a notebook and a waterproof jacket. Lunch is provided, but bring your own water. At the station, a scientist will explain how sensors measure waves. We will return to college at half past three. Please meet outside the main entrance, rather than at the sports hall.

questions.prompt: At what hour does the coach leave?
questions.explanation: The coach leaves at nine.

questions.prompt: How many minutes does the journey take?
questions.explanation: The journey takes forty minutes.

questions.prompt: What type of jacket should students bring?
questions.explanation: A waterproof jacket is requested.

questions.prompt: What do sensors measure?
questions.explanation: Sensors measure waves.

questions.prompt: Where should students meet?
questions.explanation: The guide specifies the main entrance.

title: A repair workshop
instructions: Listen without opening the transcript. Write no more than two words and/or a number for each answer. Original short practice, not a full IELTS examination.
content: Organiser: Our repair workshop is on Sunday the tenth of November at the community hall. Doors open at ten, and repairs begin at ten thirty. We can help with small electrical appliances, bicycles and clothing. We cannot repair phones. Volunteer: Do visitors need to book? Organiser: Yes. Each visitor should book one item. The suggested donation is five pounds, but payment is optional. Please use the side entrance because the front door is being painted. We finish at two in the afternoon.

questions.prompt: In which month is the workshop?
questions.explanation: The date is the tenth of November.

questions.prompt: Which items cannot be repaired?
questions.explanation: Phones are excluded.

questions.prompt: How many items should each visitor book?
questions.explanation: Each visitor should book one item.

questions.prompt: What is the suggested donation in pounds?
questions.explanation: The suggested donation is five pounds.

questions.prompt: Which entrance should visitors use?
questions.explanation: The front door is being painted.

title: Discussing a student survey
instructions: Listen without opening the transcript. Write no more than two words and/or a number for each answer. Original short practice, not a full IELTS examination.
content: Tutor: Tell me about your transport survey. Student: We invited two hundred students, but only eighty responded. Most responses came from first-year students, so the sample may not represent the whole college. Tutor: What did you ask? Student: How they travel to campus and what prevents them from cycling. Cost was not the main problem; safety was mentioned most often. Tutor: What will you do next? Student: Interview ten cyclists next week. Then we will compare the interviews with the questionnaire results. Our report is due on Friday, and it should include a chart.

questions.prompt: How many students responded?
questions.explanation: Eighty of the invited students responded.

questions.prompt: Which year supplied most responses?
questions.explanation: Most respondents were first-year students.

questions.prompt: What concern was mentioned most often?
questions.explanation: Safety was the leading concern.

questions.prompt: How many cyclists will be interviewed?
questions.explanation: The student plans ten interviews.

questions.prompt: On what day is the report due?
questions.explanation: The report is due on Friday.

title: A reusable cup trial
instructions: Use only the passage. Answer TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN. Original short practice, not a full IELTS examination.
content: A small cafe tested a reusable cup scheme for six weeks. Customers paid a refundable deposit when borrowing a cup. They could return it to either of the cafe's two branches. Staff washed returned cups before using them again. During the trial, the cafe used fewer disposable cups than in the previous six weeks. However, the manager did not calculate the environmental impact of washing and transport. Some customers said they forgot to bring cups back, so the cafe added reminder signs near the doors. The deposit amount stayed the same throughout the trial.

questions.prompt: The trial lasted six weeks.
questions.explanation: Six weeks is stated.

questions.prompt: Cups could only be returned to one branch.
questions.explanation: Either of two branches accepted returns.

questions.prompt: Staff washed cups before reusing them.
questions.explanation: Returned cups were washed.

questions.prompt: The scheme reduced total carbon emissions by half.
questions.explanation: Environmental impact was not calculated.

questions.prompt: The cafe increased its deposit during the trial.
questions.explanation: The deposit stayed the same.

title: Flexible working hours
instructions: Use only the passage. Answer TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN. Original short practice, not a full IELTS examination.
content: A design company introduced flexible starting times for a three-month trial. Employees could begin work between seven and ten, but everyone had to be available for meetings from eleven until three. The total weekly hours did not change. At the end of the trial, an anonymous survey found that many employees valued the easier commute. Managers reported that projects were still delivered on schedule. The survey did not ask about sleep, and the company did not compare productivity with other businesses. The flexible system was retained, although a small customer-support team continued using fixed shifts.

questions.prompt: Employees could start work at eight.
questions.explanation: Eight falls within the seven-to-ten starting window.

questions.prompt: Weekly working hours were reduced.
questions.explanation: Weekly hours did not change.

questions.prompt: Employees reported sleeping longer.
questions.explanation: The survey did not ask about sleep.

questions.prompt: Managers said projects arrived on schedule.
questions.explanation: Projects were delivered on schedule.

questions.prompt: Every employee moved to flexible starting times.
questions.explanation: Customer support kept fixed shifts.

title: A neighbourhood seed library
instructions: Use only the passage. Answer TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN. Original short practice, not a full IELTS examination.
content: A seed library lets residents borrow packets of seeds rather than books. At the end of the growing season, borrowers are encouraged, but not required, to return seeds collected from their plants. The project began with donations from local gardeners. Volunteers label packets with the plant name and the collection year. They also run introductory gardening sessions once a month. The organisers warn that seeds from some hybrid plants may not produce plants identical to their parents. They do not promise that every seed will germinate. A secure cabinet inside the public library keeps the packets dry.

questions.prompt: Borrowers must return seeds.
questions.explanation: Returns are encouraged, not required.

questions.prompt: Local gardeners supplied the initial seeds.
questions.explanation: The project began with gardener donations.

questions.prompt: Packet labels include the collection year.
questions.explanation: Both plant name and collection year are listed.

questions.prompt: Hybrid plants always produce identical offspring.
questions.explanation: The organisers warn that they may not.

questions.prompt: The project has more than five hundred borrowers.
questions.explanation: No borrower count is given.

title: Citizen science and river monitoring
instructions: Use only the passage. Answer TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN. Original short practice, not a full IELTS examination.
content: A river-monitoring project trains volunteers to measure water clarity. Before collecting data, every volunteer attends a practical session and compares readings with an experienced researcher. Measurements are taken at fixed locations, allowing changes over time to be compared. Heavy rain can affect clarity, so volunteers record recent weather as well. The researchers review unusual results rather than deleting them automatically. They note that cloudy water alone cannot identify a particular pollutant. Laboratory testing is needed for that purpose. The project publishes monthly summaries, but the passage does not indicate whether the river has become cleaner.

questions.prompt: Training takes place before data collection.
questions.explanation: Every volunteer attends training first.

questions.prompt: Volunteers choose new locations every month.
questions.explanation: Measurements use fixed locations.

questions.prompt: Recent weather is recorded.
questions.explanation: Weather is recorded because rain affects clarity.

questions.prompt: Cloudy water identifies a specific pollutant.
questions.explanation: Laboratory testing is required.

questions.prompt: The river is now cleaner than last year.
questions.explanation: No improvement over time is reported.

content: Describe a place where you like to relax. Say where it is, how often you go, what you do there, and why it helps you relax. Follow-up: Why do cities need quiet public spaces? Can relaxation be taught?

title: Starting point: booking a study room

title: Starting point: a walking group
instructions: Use only the passage. Answer TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN. Original short practice, not a full IELTS examination.
content: A neighbourhood walking group meets every Saturday morning at the railway station. The walks last about an hour and are open to adults of all fitness levels. No payment is required. A volunteer chooses the route each week, avoiding busy roads where possible. If heavy rain is forecast, the organiser sends a cancellation message on Friday evening. Participants are advised to wear comfortable shoes and bring water. The group has not collected information about changes in participants' health.

questions.prompt: The group meets on Saturdays.
questions.explanation: Saturday morning is stated.

questions.prompt: Participants must pay for each walk.
questions.explanation: No payment is required.

questions.prompt: The same route is used every week.
questions.explanation: A route is chosen each week but repetition is not specified.

questions.prompt: The group may cancel because of heavy rain.
questions.explanation: A cancellation is sent when heavy rain is forecast.

questions.prompt: The walks have improved participants' health.
questions.explanation: Health changes have not been recorded.

title: Vocabulary: environment
instructions: Choose the best word from the word bank for each gap and type it. Each word is used once; some words are extra. This is an original vocabulary exercise, not a Cambridge or IELTS test.
content:
Word bank: mitigate, sustainable, emissions, conserve, habitat, fragile, dispose

Topic: environment and climate. Many IELTS tasks discuss how people can protect the natural world.

questions.prompt: Planting trees along busy roads is one way to ____ the effects of traffic pollution.
questions.explanation: To mitigate means to make something less severe.

questions.prompt: Farmers are encouraged to use ____ methods that protect the soil for future generations.
questions.explanation: Sustainable describes something that can continue without causing long-term damage.

questions.prompt: Factories must report their carbon ____ to the government every year.
questions.explanation: Emissions are gases released into the air.

questions.prompt: Turning off lights when leaving a room helps households ____ energy.
questions.explanation: To conserve is to use carefully and avoid waste.

questions.prompt: Draining the wetland destroyed the ____ of many rare birds.
questions.explanation: A habitat is the natural home of an animal or plant.

title: Vocabulary: education and work
instructions: Choose the best word from the word bank for each gap and type it. Each word is used once; some words are extra. This is an original vocabulary exercise, not a Cambridge or IELTS test.
content:
Word bank: curriculum, qualification, deadline, collaborate, flexible, tuition, mentor

Topic: education and employment. These words are common in discussions about studying and careers.

questions.prompt: The school is updating its ____ to include more practical science lessons.
questions.explanation: A curriculum is the set of subjects taught in a course or school.

questions.prompt: A teaching ____ is usually needed before you can work in a state school.
questions.explanation: A qualification is a certificate or degree showing you have completed training.

questions.prompt: Students who miss the ____ for the essay lose marks.
questions.explanation: A deadline is the latest time by which something must be done.

questions.prompt: Engineers and designers often ____ on projects so that ideas can be shared.
questions.explanation: To collaborate is to work together with others.

questions.prompt: Many employees prefer ____ hours, such as starting earlier or later.
questions.explanation: Flexible means able to change to suit different needs.

title: Vocabulary: technology and society
instructions: Choose the best word from the word bank for each gap and type it. Each word is used once; some words are extra. This is an original vocabulary exercise, not a Cambridge or IELTS test.
content:
Word bank: innovation, privacy, automate, access, reliable, obsolete, virtual

Topic: technology and society. These words help you discuss the benefits and risks of new tools.

questions.prompt: Many people worry about their online ____ when apps collect personal data.
questions.explanation: Privacy is the right to keep personal information protected.

questions.prompt: Robots can ____ repetitive tasks in factories, reducing the need for manual work.
questions.explanation: To automate is to make a process work by machine with little human effort.

questions.prompt: Rural villages often lack broadband ____, so students cannot easily study online.
questions.explanation: Access means the ability to reach or use something.

questions.prompt: A ____ internet connection is essential for video lessons, because interruptions waste time.
questions.explanation: Reliable means dependable and working consistently.

questions.prompt: Medical ____ has helped doctors to detect illnesses earlier.
questions.explanation: Innovation is the introduction of new ideas or methods.

title: Vocabulary: health and lifestyle
instructions: Choose the best word from the word bank for each gap and type it. Each word is used once; some words are extra. This is an original vocabulary exercise, not a Cambridge or IELTS test.
content:
Word bank: sedentary, nutrition, chronic, moderate, stress, contagious, vaccine

Topic: health and lifestyle. These words are useful for describing habits and wellbeing.

questions.prompt: Office workers with a ____ lifestyle should stand up and walk regularly.
questions.explanation: Sedentary means involving a lot of sitting and little movement.

questions.prompt: Good ____ means eating a balanced diet with enough vitamins and protein.
questions.explanation: Nutrition is the food and nutrients the body needs.

questions.prompt: Diabetes is a ____ condition that people usually manage for many years.
questions.explanation: Chronic describes a condition that lasts a long time.

questions.prompt: Doctors recommend ____ exercise, such as brisk walking, for thirty minutes a day.
questions.explanation: Moderate means medium in amount or intensity, not extreme.

questions.prompt: Taking short breaks can help students manage ____ before exams.
questions.explanation: Stress is mental or emotional pressure.
